title: Payment-Record Courtesy on HomeFlood Final Settlements
content:
**Rule.** The closing payment on a cancelled HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy carries a payment-record courtesy. It looks at the notices of cancellation for nonpayment (NONPAYMENT) ever mailed on the policy, and at how long the policy had been in force on the payment date. That length is counted in whole calendar months from the policy's effective date.

| Nonpayment notices ever mailed on the policy | In force on the payment date | Courtesy |
|---|---|---|
| none | at least 60 whole months | 15 USD |
| none | fewer than 60 whole months | 5 USD |
| one or more | any | none |

**Form of the courtesy.** The courtesy is an amount taken off the closing payment.

**The payment date.** The payment date is the day the customer makes the closing payment, and every length of time counted to the payment date ends on that day. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

**Which notices count.** Notices for material misrepresentation and non-renewal notices are not nonpayment notices and do not count.

*Hypothetical cases:*
- A policy in force for 7 years with no nonpayment notice: 15.00.
- A policy in force for 2 years with no nonpayment notice: 5.00.
- A policy with one nonpayment notice that was later rescinded: none. The notice was still mailed.
